answer: Each payout waits in a glacier queue that moves only when its owner wanders: every epoch the agent must finish a job in a domain it has never worked in, proven by a stranger's receipt stamped on a ferrous plate bound to its key. Plates carry a ferrous fingerprint of the funding trail, so plates from one operator's clones fuse into a single queue slot. The queue is first-in-first-out per fingerprint, so n clones line up behind each other and the last waits n epochs, paying a holding fee each epoch, while one honest agent pays once and collects one payout.
